claims.statement: For each favorable leaf v with i_p(T-v)>0, the selector Delta_p(T-v)<0 is equivalent to the mean addability of a uniform independent p-set of T-v being less than p+1. The desired v-summand is an adjacent-rank difference in the distinct marked slice of H_v; this translation does not establish a coupling or inequality between those measures, so it yields no resolution of the global lower-region aggregate.
claims.scope: Exact probability reformulation for finite ordinary trees and eligible (T,p), using the fixed favorable selector and the original leaf data; partial only.
claims.reason: Double-counting addable vertices gives the selector's expectation identity exactly. The marked extension count exposes the different conditioned rank measure and its multiple-mark correction, but no justified bridge transfers the selector bound to the complete selected sum.

limitations: No proof of the global deficit budget or complete aggregate inequality is obtained.
No eligible ordinary-tree counterexample is produced.
The expectation comparison is valid only when the corresponding rank set count is nonzero; the algebraic selector identity itself remains valid with zero extension.
